idea: Simple ways to protect plumbing during renovation
title: How to Protect Your Pipes During a Home Renovation
description: During a renovation, drywall dust, tile grout, and construction rubble frequently fall into open waste lines, hardening into severe blockages deep inside your plumbing system. Always seal exposed pipe openings immediately after demolition or rough-in work. Use mechanical expansion test plugs or solvent-weld temporary caps on open drain lines, and keep plastic plaster guards mounted over rough-in shower valves. Avoid washing paint brushes, spackle tools, or thin-set mortar into household sinks. Protecting pipe openings during construction prevents costly drain clearing service calls once your beautiful new space is completed.
image_prompt: A realistic professional photograph of a residential bathroom undergoing renovation, captured in a vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. In the center foreground, a 2-inch white PVC waste drain pipe extends upward from a unfinished concrete subfloor. The top open end of the PVC pipe is securely sealed with a bright orange rubber expansion test plug with a zinc-plated metal wing nut tightened on top. Around the floor near the pipe base are fine particles of drywall dust and small tile chips, demonstrating that the plug is blocking debris from entering the pipe. The background softly shows exposed wooden wall studs and rough-in water lines in natural daylight.
